elements.element: Renewal must use either of the permitted structures: renewal only by mutual written agreement or automatic renewal subject to the applicable preferred requirements.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 uses the permitted automatic-renewal structure.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be twelve months.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 states that each Order Form renews for twelve months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must be able to opt out on thirty days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 permits either Party, including Customer, to prevent renewal by giving thirty days' advance written notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide a reminder sixty days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no renewal-reminder obligation. The ninety-day notice in Section 8.3 applies only to fee increases and is not a renewal reminder.

elements.element: Renewal price increases must be capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 expressly caps recurring Fee increases at the lesser of the preceding twelve-month CPI increase and three percent.
Section 8.2 provides for automatic twelve-month renewal unless notice is given.

elements.element: The non-renewal notice period must be no more than sixty days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires thirty days' advance written notice, which is within the sixty-day maximum.

elements.element: Renewal price increases must not exceed five percent.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps increases at the lesser of CPI and three percent, necessarily no more than five percent.

result.reason: The redline makes the single change needed to bring the non-renewal period within tolerance and leaves the already-compliant price cap intact. It fully satisfies the fallback and most of the automatic-renewal preferred structure, but it does not impose the required sixty-day Vendor renewal reminder. The operative language remains clear and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
